proof.criterion: AC1 — in a role container where the repository's packages are not installed, no command the repository tells an agent to run reports a passing lint, including in a container where a plain `bunx biome` has already fetched the squatted package into bun's own cache.
proof.surface: This issue's own role container (worker image, bun 1.3.14), the shared workspace with no node_modules, poisoned first by one `bunx biome check .`, which left /tmp/bunx-1000-biome@latest behind.
proof.command: bunx biome check . ; bunx biome --version ; bunx --no-install biome check . ; bun run lint packages/pi-legion/ ; bun run typecheck ; (cd packages/pi-legion && bun run lint) ; scripts/repo-tool.sh biome check .
proof.observed: Every command the repository now prescribes exits 1 with the wrapper's message — `repo-tool: biome is not installed` or `tsc is not installed`, the two paths tried (./node_modules/.bin/<tool> and the repository root's) and the remedy naming `bun install` and scripts/legion-setup.sh. Nothing reports a check it did not run.
proof.negativeControl: In that same container the pre-change form `bunx biome check .` exits 0 having checked no file, `bunx biome --version` answers 0.3.3 (the squatted package, not the pinned Biome 2.4.11), and `bunx --no-install biome check .` also exits 0 once the plain form has run once there — the state the spec says the failure needs.

proof.criterion: AC2 — the required lint job fails if the vulnerable form reappears in any file that prescribes a command for lint, types or tests.
proof.surface: `.github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh` on the real tree and its own harness (a miniature repository per case with the real script symlinked in), as CI's required lint and test jobs run them; the lint job itself passed on this head (run 39558307948, job lint, 3m8s).
proof.observed: The guard exits 0 with `every prescribed biome, tsc, tsserver and playwright command runs through scripts/repo-tool.sh (13 manifest(s), 8 workflow(s), 92 shell script(s), 536 guide(s))`; its suite reports `Results: 53 passed, 0 failed`.
proof.negativeControl: `bunx biome check <package>/` put back into AGENTS.md's commands block and into packages/contracts' lint recipe: the guard exits 1 naming `packages/contracts/package.json:41` and `AGENTS.md:52`, each with its reason. Both files were restored byte-for-byte afterwards (jj diff --stat unchanged).

proof.criterion: AC3 (pre-merge proxy) — the packages are in place, the lint command answers with the version bun.lock pins and its `Checked N files` line, nothing of the install is on the container's own filesystem, and the workspace's tracked files, bun.lock among them, are unchanged by it.
proof.surface: A throwaway copy of this tree on the issue volume (/legion/workspaces/infra-71-proof), with no node_modules and a cold cache, run exactly as the deployment's setup line runs it. The full line — a role container created after the deployment names the script, before the agent's first turn — is the production check.
proof.command: env LEGION_WORKSPACE=/legion/workspaces/infra-71-proof LEGION_ISSUE=INFRA-71 LEGION_ROLE=implementer LEGION_GENERATION=1 LEGION_STATE_DIR=/legion/proof-state sh scripts/legion-setup.sh ; ./node_modules/.bin/biome --version ; bun run lint . ; cksum bun.lock ; find /tmp $HOME -newer <a marker taken just before the run>
proof.observed: Exit 0 after `1986 packages installed [29.01s]` from a cold cache. node_modules/.bin/biome is `Version: 2.4.11`, the version bun.lock pins, and `bun run lint .` prints `Checked 1079 files in 33s`. `cksum bun.lock` is 581893351 340936 before and after. The cache (1,395,623,403 bytes) and the lock, log and marker are on the issue volume; no report is written. The container's own disk took exactly one empty file, /tmp/.<hex>-00000000.hm (0 bytes, bun's own temp), and nothing else: ~/.bun and ~/.cache/bun are byte-identical before and after (113,086,919 and 1,605,253 bytes — the squatted package the AC1 control fetched, not this install's). A second run with BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR set, as an issue pod now sets it, installs into that directory (1,395,645,249 bytes there) and makes none of its own.
proof.negativeControl: In that same copy immediately before the run, `bun run lint .` exits 1 with the wrapper's `biome is not installed` message.

proof.criterion: AC4 — a role whose install failed still starts, with what failed in front of its agent in its first turn.
proof.surface: The same throwaway copy with failures injected, and a real Oh My Pi pane (LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp, pi-shared's omp harness `runLegionPane`, this checkout's two plugins).
proof.command: LEGION_SETUP_INSTALL_TIMEOUT=1 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh ; BUN_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:1/ sh scripts/legion-setup.sh with the cache moved aside ; LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_WAIT=1 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh against a held lock ; bun test on a throwaway runLegionPane case that writes the report into the pane's LEGION_STATE_DIR
proof.observed: Every injection exits 0, leaves no marker, and writes $LEGION_STATE_DIR/legion-setup-report.json carrying this run's issue, role and generation: `install-timeout` with exitStatus 124; `install-failed` with exitStatus 1 and a 999-character bounded detail; `lock-timeout` after 1.1 s. On the real binary, the pane whose report matches its own issue, role and generation carries `Legion's setup command could not install this repository's packages`, the reason, and the `sh scripts/legion-setup.sh` retry in its first turn's provider request.
proof.negativeControl: The same pane with a report whose generation is 9 rather than its own carries no such text (2 pass, 0 fail across the pair), and a successful run deletes a stale report, leaving 0 files in the state directory. AC4's daemon half — no launch failure charged, no worker-died, the issue not held — is daemon behaviour conditioned on exit 0 and is the production check.

proof.criterion: AC5 — a second role of the same issue, starting while the packages are already there, installs nothing (restated per the plan's departure 3 against the issue's one shared cache).
proof.surface: The same throwaway copy, a second run under another role's identity after a successful one.
proof.command: du -sb /legion/bun/cache ; env LEGION_ROLE=reviewer … sh scripts/legion-setup.sh ; du -sb /legion/bun/cache ; find node_modules -newer /legion/bun/state/installed | wc -l
proof.observed: `this bun.lock's packages are already installed; nothing to do` in 0.053 s, exit 0; the shared cache is byte-identical across the run (1,395,623,403 bytes before and after); bun is never run; 0 files under node_modules are newer than the marker.
proof.negativeControl: Remove node_modules/.bin/biome and run again: the marker alone does not satisfy the guard and it installs (`Checked 1009 installs across 1200 packages`).

trickyParts: The shared workspace is deliberately left WITHOUT node_modules: AC1's state is the uninstalled one, every later role of this issue mounts this workspace, and installing here would destroy the state the tester must reproduce. Every install proof ran in a throwaway copy on the issue volume, which was removed at the end of the phase.

To reproduce AC1's state, poison the container first with one `bunx biome check .` in the workspace, which leaves /tmp/bunx-<uid>-biome@latest. Without it the plain form behaves the same, but `bunx --no-install biome check .` refuses rather than passing, and the spec's point is that it passes once the plain form has run.

The container has no PyYAML on python3's default path, so the repository's python guards cannot be run here as CI runs them. A copy extracted at /legion/pytools with PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools runs them; check-image-trigger-paths.sh sets PYTHONPATH itself, so it needs a symlink in .github/scripts for the one run (removed afterwards). CI's runner has PyYAML, so no script changed for this.

A bun install run by hand in a role container must name BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR on the issue volume: the default cache lands on the container's own ephemeral disk, whose breach evicts the whole pod. The notice's retry advice therefore names the script and not a bare `bun install`.
